risks.basis: the same app (stonedesk) has this defect on record
risks.risk: stonedesk.html's Admin Overview 'Storage Used' KPI computed Math.min(100, Math.round((totalBytes/1024/5120)*100)) and wrote it into a card labelled only 'Storage Used'. THE FLAGGED Math.min IS THE ONE PART THAT WAS RIGHT and is recorded as a FALSE POSITIVE for the overrun-inversion class: a localStorage quota is a hard ceiling, a write past it throws, so the ratio cannot legitimately exceed 1 and the cap could never hide an overrun. The two real defects were beside it. (1) THE DENOMINATOR WAS ASSUMED: 5120 KB is a guess at the browser quota, real quotas vary by browser and origin, and where the true quota is larger this reported a half-used store as FULL -- a number an owner acts on, by deleting data, from the two delete buttons on the same panel. (2) THE POPULATION WAS NOT THE ONE THE LABEL NAMED: the loop sums EVERY key in localStorage, which on this platform is every SAIRN app in the browser, and presented it as StoneDesk's -- while the paragraph eleven lines below the card draws exactly that distinction for the delete buttons ('removes only what StoneDesk stored -- other SAIRN apps in this browser are untouched'). So the card showed a percentage of a guess over another app's data. Fixed to report the measured bytes with the label naming the population; the percentage returns when navigator.storage.estimate() is wired with a real quota rather than a constant. Regression suite written first with a known-bad control that restores both halves in a copy and requires two arms red, file restored byte-identical.

risks.basis: the same app (stonedesk) has this defect on record

Two things were still wrong with the figure. (1) `.length * 2` assumes two bytes per UTF-16 code unit, which is wrong for an astral character (a surrogate pair is two units) and is not how every engine charges its quota, so the total is an approximation presented as a measurement. (2) THE KEYS WERE NOT COUNTED AT ALL -- only the values -- and keys are stored too, so the figure was biased DOWN, which is the wrong direction for a number somebody reads as 'how full am I'. Keys are now included and the value carries a `~`, a mark on the number rather than a longer label because the card has room for a figure and not a sentence. AND THE QUOTA SEARCH IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: no storage_quota, storage_limit, quota_bytes or max_storage exists anywhere in the repo's .js, .sql, .json or .html, and vercel.json carries no storage configuration. It would not help if it did -- this KPI counts BROWSER localStorage, which neither Supabase nor Vercel governs, and the browser's own limit varies by engine and origin and is not knowable synchronously. So no percentage is computed and none is invented.

A throw from either -- the realm missing the helper, a toast implementation changed, an unexpected value -- therefore reported a credential THE SERVER HAD ALREADY CREATED as a network failure. risks.risk: api/bridge.js's dispatch fell through to handlePush for EVERY unknown ?action=, so a request naming an action that has never existed was answered 401 NO_LICENCE or 403 -- a credential diagnosis for a routing fault. THREE LIVE CALL SITES land there, measured by grepping every app file for the URL rather than reasoned about: stonedesk.html:12814 (?action=maps-static), :12927 (?action=maps-optimize), and :7795, which sends no action and no data_type and a sairn-mobile-sync envelope body, reaches handlePush and UPSERTS a bridge_data row of {jobs:null, invoices:null, employees:null}. The wrong-layer diagnosis is the same class Guardian check 30 records costing a session a hunt for a RESEND_API_KEY that was present and correct the whole time; the null-row write is a silent failure, swallowed by a bare .catch(). FIX: KNOWN_ACTIONS = [push, proxy_get], spelled once, with the 400 UNKNOWN_ACTION refusal DERIVING its message from that array so a fourth action cannot be added to the gate without the message following. `pull` is deliberately absent and an arm asserts the absence -- it was removed 2026-09-17 for serving one tenant's data to an unauthenticated GET keyed on a RAW LICENCE KEY, and a refusal that advertises a withdrawn read side is worse than no refusal. ARMS: api/b21-bridge-unknown-action.test.js, 14 arms 0 failed, including the negative control the defect needs (a LICENCE-HEADED and SESSION-HEADED POST to an unknown action returns 400 and writes ZERO rows -- the valid credentials are the point, because without them a 401 arrives whether the refusal exists or not), A4 (an unauthenticated unknown action is still UNKNOWN_ACTION and never NO_LICENCE), C1-C3 controls proving the one live push caller and both proxy_get spellings still work, and E1 ABLATION (guard cut from a lifted copy -> the unknown action reaches handlePush and upserts, the pre-fix behaviour reproduced) with E2 CLEAN proving the ablation is a removal and not a corrupted file. NOT CLOSED BY THIS FIX, declared rather than left to be found: an ABSENT ?action= is still accepted and still reaches handlePush (arm D1 asserts that residual on purpose), and the three CALLERS are unchanged because stonedesk.html is held by fourth under a live b34 claim -- routed as an open-work row instead. UNVERIFIED LIVE: the refusal is not deployed at the time of this record, so every arm is against the handler and none against the URL.
